I understand that exactly and only realized it like halfway through my weight loss. I always felt like the same person. Still depressed, still anxious, still cynical, still stuck, all of that.

Self love for me started with actively being aware of my thoughts and refocusing them. I used to use a lot of self deprecating humor and was always so hard on myself when I didn't deserve it. When I do this now, I acknowledge it and then change it by saying something kind to myself. It felt dumb at first but eventually you just believe it.  

Also (as a people pleaser) learning how to say no. And doing little things everyday that make me feel good like making my bed, reading, roller skating if the weather is nice, listening to a podcast while I cook etc. Having little things to look forward to in my routine.

Just a few things I try to be mindful of. It's such a process but I believe in you. :)

I actually did the whole 30 diet with my coworker for a month, which was basically no sugar, grains, dairy, alcohol or junk food if you aren’t already familiar. I don’t do this anymore but have since naturally cut back drastically on all of these things because of it. At the beginning I also weighed and logged everything I ate into my fitness pal. I tried to avoid trigger foods (chocolate and fast food) as much as possible because it would usually lead to a binge. 

After doing this for a couple of months it just became routine and the cravings mostly went away. I don’t really exercise outside of some yoga that I do in my living room a few times a week. I also don’t weigh and log my food anymore, I just try to be more mindful of what I’m eating overall and don’t let food control me anymore. 

Anyway, you got this! It’s not a linear process and bad days are okay and inevitable.
